name: Eton crop

lead: The Eton crop is a close-cropped, slicked-down hairstyle that became popular in the 1920s. By leaving little hair, it shows off the ears, neck and facial structure.
It is a historical style that continues to be referenced in modern cropped cuts. No studies have examined it.

paras: The hair is cut close at the top, sides and back, then slicked flat with a pomade-type product. Regular trims keep the lines sharp.
There are no health risks; the main consideration is that the cut is short and regrows slowly.

chain: Hair cropped close and slicked flat
Ears, neck and skull shape fully visible
Cheekbones and jaw take centre stage
angle.text: With little hair to frame the face, the look draws attention to bone structure and features. It is typically paired with strong features or earrings.

lead: The Eton crop is a very short, slicked-down women's hairstyle. It is named for a cut associated with schoolboys at Eton College and became mainstream in the mid-1920s.[1][2]
It showed off the shape of cloche hats and was worn by figures including Josephine Baker and Bessie Love.[1][2] Its exposed ears and neck make facial structure the focus of the look.

paras: The cut is trimmed very close, with a slightly longer top, and slicked flat to produce a glossy finish.[2] Earlier short bobs were worn in the 1910s by Irene Castle, Coco Chanel and Polaire, and the Eton crop followed in the 1920s.[1] Critic Margot Asquith mocked the style in 1927, and it was favoured by many masculine lesbians in England.[1]

timeline.event: Early bobs worn by Irene Castle, Coco Chanel and Polaire.[1]
The Eton crop becomes mainstream by the mid-1920s.[1]
